paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's people went looking for safety everywhere except with God. They set out for Egypt "without asking My advice" (Isaiah 30:2), and Egypt turned out to be a people who bring "neither help nor benefit" (Isaiah 30:5). When we run to a plan before we run to the LORD, we end up hauling our treasure through lions and vipers to a place that can't help us.

Now look at what makes this one sting. The people didn't just skip God's advice, they told the prophets, "Speak to us pleasant words" (Isaiah 30:10). Friend, I get it. A comfortable word feels good right up until the wall comes down! But a pleasant lie is a crack in the wall you keep painting over, and the Holy One of Israel loves His people too much to just paint.

And here's the part I want you to carry out of my bakery. Right in the middle of all that trouble, the Lord GOD hands them the way out: "By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence" (Isaiah 30:15). The door was open. They just weren't willing. So the next time you're tempted to grab the swift horse and run, baker, turn around, listen to His word, and rest in Him instead.
